facts.text: Gillette sprang to life in 1891 when the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad extended its tracks to the area, naming the new town after surveyor Edward Gillette.
Before its 1891 founding, the settlement was known as Donkey Town, a name taken from nearby Donkey Creek.
Gillette brands itself the Energy Capital of the Nation, a nod to Wyoming’s contribution of almost 35 percent of the country’s coal.
The city hosts a public library that serves as a branch of the Campbell County Public Library System, keeping residents connected to books and community events.
Travel Stories lets visitors take virtual tours of downtown Gillette, uncovering the town’s history from the comfort of their car.
Gillette stands as the county seat of Campbell County, Wyoming, anchoring the region’s government and civic life.
